newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee pulls back further, but uptrend holds.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee pulls back further, but uptrend holds.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures pulled back further in the afternoon to end Friday broadly lower in correction to Thursday's dazzling rally to a 20-month peak.
Floor sources said the slide followed fund long liquidation as well as pre-weekend profit-taking. "The market has gone up so much. It needs a bit of correction," said one.

Despite today's setback, traders said the overall uptrend remained intact and the market could climb again especially if there are strong fears of frost in Brazil in the coming weeks. "The market is still friendly to me," said one trader.
Benchmark July contract fell to end sharply down at $2,465 a tonne, down $135, and near the day's low of $2,455.
Its intraday high was $2,660 but failed to match Thursday's 20-month peak of $2,670.
July surged by $300-$400 a tonne in one session on Thursday but the contract was still considered cheap in relation to the premium arabicas on the New York futures.
The perception of robustas being well under-valued attracted strong demand by roasters eager to step up use of robustas in the blends in order to help offset the steep arabica costs.
The interest in second half 1997 robustas also spilled over to the cash market where it dominated business in major consuming countries.
LIFFE's first-position May expired at lunchtime at $2,505, up just $5 on the day. A total of 1,367 five-tonne-lots were tendered against May and a further 645 were re-tenders, LIFFE said.
Futures volume reached 9,236 lots and active July/Sept switches dominated the activity. The spread was traded at $33-$35.
Options trade saw another brisk day, with some 2,342 lots changing hands.
But options traders said nervous investors were now turning to puts after at least two solid weeks of call buying.
"There's been minimal call interest because people are worried prices will slip off," said one options broker.
In fundamental news, private U.S. forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Friday temperatures in Brazil's coffee belt would be below normal through Sunday but no damaging cold was expected.
